clue.text: Get better phoning old explorer

indicators.note: phoning suggests speech down a line, so the word is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: to get better after illness or a slump is to rally

explanation.surface: Someone recovering from illness rings up a long-dead adventurer.
explanation.walkthrough: The surname is traditionally pronounced like 'rally', which is what makes 'phoning' work.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Walter Raleigh was an Elizabethan adventurer who sailed to the Americas, an explorer of long ago.

clue.text: That is right — one that's managed at the top

definitions.text: That is right — one that's managed at the top

indicators.note: at the top puts that piece first in this down answer

parts.note: ran a business is managed it
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A tribute to a football boss who took his side to the summit of the league.
explanation.walkthrough: Claudio Ranieri managed Leicester City to the 2015-16 Premier League title, so the whole clue also describes him.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue as a whole pictures a manager who led his club to first place, which Ranieri did with Leicester.

clue.text: Result of depression whilst husband's away? Could be

definitions.text: Result of depression whilst husband's away? Could be

indicators.note: Could be hints that the remaining letters can be rearranged into another phrase
is away means this letter is gone from the words

explanation.surface: A wife suggests her gloom is down to her husband being absent.
explanation.walkthrough: Take H from DEPRESSION WHILST and rearrange the rest; read whole, the clue also describes the gloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling down and dispirited is exactly what depression, or a lonely spell, produces.

clue.text: Current clue can't possibly impress

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

indicators.note: possibly says the letters could be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: A setter fears a current clue is unlikely to make an impression.
explanation.definitionFit: To inculcate an idea is to instil it by repetition, fixing it in someone's mind.

clue.text: Couple in difficulty

definitions.meaning: to couple a trailer to a car is to fasten or hook it on

explanation.surface: A pair of people find themselves in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to hook a trailer on and a snag holding things up.

clue.text: Official: Domino's backing employee

indicators.note: backing means the combined letters are read from the end to the start

parts.note: a referee, or ref, is a match official
Fats Domino was the American rock-and-roll pianist and singer

explanation.surface: A notice about the pizza chain Domino's supporting one of its workers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Domino's' looks like the pizza company; it is the singer Fats Domino, so the possessive hides his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: A staffer is a member of the staff of an organisation, a worker on its payroll.

clue.text: Fat tax mentioned — thin on top!

indicators.note: on top puts that piece first in this down answer

parts.note: spare can mean lean or thin, as in a spare frame

indicators.note: mentioned says the word is spoken, so a soundalike is wanted

parts.note: to tire is to tax or wear out

explanation.surface: A complaint about a levy on fat, from someone going bald.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tax' is not a levy but the verb meaning tire, which is said like TYRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A spare tyre is a roll of flab around the waist, a jokey name for belly fat.

clue.text: Bill's fellow rider

parts.note: an ad, or advertisement, is a bill posted up
a don is a fellow of a university college

explanation.surface: Bill's companion on a horse or bike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rider' looks like a horseman; it is an extra clause attached to a document.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider is an extra provision tacked onto a bill or contract, something attached on.

clue.text: Animal lover from country's said nothing — beast is providing lifts outside

indicators.note: said means the possessive is spoken, giving a name that sounds the same

parts.note: France's is the possessive of the country
O is zero, nothing

indicators.note: outside puts the upturned piece around the others
lifts means read upwards in this down answer

parts.note: providing means if, as in 'providing it rains'
an ass is a beast of burden

explanation.surface: An account of a donkey being hoisted around a country, a little absurdly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifts' reads as hoisting the beast; in a down answer it means read upwards, and 'outside' wraps that upturned piece round the beast and 'is'. 'country's said' sounds like the saint's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Francis of Assisi is the patron saint of animals, famous for preaching to birds.

clue.text: Turned another colour after swallowing tablet and looking upset

indicators.note: swallowing says the tablet goes inside the other word

parts.note: redyed means dyed again, changed in colour
E is slang for an ecstasy tablet

explanation.surface: Someone changes colour after taking a pill and looks distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyes reddened by crying or lack of sleep make a person look distressed.

clue.text: Unprecedented tax on fat man's in force here

parts.note: something unprecedented has never happened before, so it is new
scot is an old word for a tax or levy, as in scot-free

indicators.note: in says the man's name sits inside the word for fat

parts.note: lard is pig fat used in cooking
Andy is a man's name

explanation.surface: A novel levy on an overweight man is being enforced in this place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' just joins the pieces; 'man's' reads as 'man is', so the man is in the fat.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotland Yard is the headquarters of London's Metropolitan Police, so it is where that police force is based.

clue.text: Get rid of old car that won't start

parts.note: ex- means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: a car that won't start here loses its first letter

parts.note: Opel is a German car make

explanation.surface: Advice to scrap an old banger that refuses to start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'won't start' sounds like a flat battery; it means dropping the first letter of the car make.
explanation.definitionFit: To expel is to drive out or eject, so getting rid of someone or something.

clue.text: Noisy protest extremely unchristian — head dished out a hundred lines

indicators.note: dished out suggests the letters are served up in a new arrangement
extremely means only the extreme letters, first and last, of unchristian are used

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
RY is short for railway, a system of lines

explanation.surface: A headteacher, rather uncharitably, punishes a pupil with a hundred lines.
explanation.walkthrough: Lines in the surface are a school punishment; here they are railway lines.
explanation.definitionFit: A hue and cry is a loud public outcry or clamour of objection.

clue.text: Truly settled? I yearn to move out!

indicators.note: out puts the rearranged letters outside the word for settled
to move tells us the letters of I yearn are shifted about

parts.note: a bird that has settled on a branch has lit there

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether they are really settled, while longing to move house.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged I YEARN goes round LIT.
explanation.definitionFit: In reality means actually or in fact, an adverb just like truly.

clue.text: Embarrassing situation — knight pulled groin limbo dancing

indicators.note: dancing tells us the remaining letters jig into a new order
pulled means the letter is drawn out of the word it sits in

parts.note: N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A knight strains his groin attempting the limbo, which is awkward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulled groin' reads as an injury; 'pulled' is the deletion signal for N.
explanation.definitionFit: An imbroglio is a confused, embarrassing entanglement or tangle of trouble.

clue.text: Thought of money spent

parts.note: spent can mean used up, as in a spent cartridge

explanation.surface: Someone reflects on money that has been spent.
explanation.definitionFit: To muse is to ponder or reflect, so mused is the past tense, thought deeply.

clue.text: Bad boy's crimes affected social worker

indicators.note: affected means altered, so the letters are changed round

parts.note: an ant is a social insect and a worker

explanation.surface: A delinquent's offences have taken a toll on his social worker.
explanation.walkthrough: A social worker is not a case officer but an ant.
explanation.definitionFit: A miscreant is a wrongdoer or villain, a person who behaves badly.

clue.text: Free … or the BBC's heading for extinction

indicators.note: the head, or first letter, is the one that dies out

parts.note: Auntie is a nickname for the BBC

explanation.surface: A worry that the BBC is heading towards extinction.
explanation.walkthrough: The BBC is Britain's public broadcaster, affectionately called 'Auntie'. 'heading for extinction' looks like doom; it means its first letter goes.
explanation.definitionFit: To untie something is to unfasten it and set it loose, a verb meaning release.

clue.text: Being useless, essentially without instrument

indicators.note: without means outside, so the core goes around the other piece
essentially keeps only the essence, the core, of the word for useless

parts.note: futile means useless
ens is a philosophical term for being or existence

explanation.surface: Being of no use, at heart, without a tool.
explanation.walkthrough: FUTILE loses its ends to give UTIL, which goes outside ENS; 'without' here means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A utensil is a tool or implement, especially one used in the kitchen.

clue.text: Drinking straight from jugs

parts.note: jugs is slang for a woman's bosom, so the drinker is a baby nursed by its mother

explanation.surface: Someone swigs from the jug instead of using a glass.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a pub drinker; the jugs are breasts and the drinker is a baby.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby fed at the breast takes milk directly from its mother, the slang sense of jugs.

clue.text: County female finished on top

indicators.note: on top puts that piece first in this down answer

parts.note: done means finished
gal is informal for a girl or woman

explanation.surface: A woman of the county comes out on top in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Donegal is a county in the far north-west of Ireland.

clue.text: Nurse gets to make short work of a repressed policeman

parts.note: EN is an enrolled nurse

indicators.note: repressed says the a is held down inside the other word

parts.note: to devour food is to eat it up quickly

explanation.surface: A nurse is told to deal swiftly with an inhibited police officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets to' only joins. The policeman is Endeavour Morse, the TV detective in Inspector Morse and its prequel Endeavour.
explanation.definitionFit: Endeavour is the first name of Inspector Morse, the fictional Oxford police detective.

clue.text: Inclined to be a fool about left

indicators.note: about says the word for fool goes round the letter

parts.note: tit is British slang for a fool

explanation.surface: Someone is prone to be a fool about leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Atilt means tilted or leaning, so inclined at an angle.

clue.text: Liberal dons feel sorry for king … and queen?

indicators.note: dons means puts on like a coat, so one word wears the other

parts.note: to rue is to regret or feel sorry
R is for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician pities the king, and perhaps the queen.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a queen is just one example of a sovereign.
explanation.definitionFit: A queen regnant is a reigning monarch, one example of a sovereign who governs.

clue.text: Turning in one's irritation increased

indicators.note: Turning says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone's annoyance has grown as they twist about in frustration.
explanation.walkthrough: No word says 'hidden' here: the letters sit across 'one's irritation' and 'Turning' reverses them.
explanation.definitionFit: Prices that have gone up have risen, so the past participle matches increased.

clue.text: I slapped Alice's bum — no good and not a logical way to win an argument

definitions.text: not a logical way to win an argument

indicators.note: bum as an adjective means poor or faulty, so the letters are messed up

explanation.surface: A confession of smacking Alice's bottom, followed by an admission that it settles nothing in a dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bum' looks like the part slapped; it is the anagram signal, and 'Alice's' reads as 'Alice has'.
explanation.definitionFit: Special pleading is arguing one-sidedly, citing favourable points and ignoring the rest, a recognised fallacy in debate.

clue.text: Country house like this cut rent, previously

indicators.note: previously places the rent piece before the house piece
cut says the second piece slices into the first

parts.note: to let a property is to rent it out
so can mean in this way, as in 'do it so'

explanation.surface: A rent reduction at a country house, as it used to be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country house' reads as a stately home, but 'Country' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lesotho is a small kingdom in southern Africa, entirely surrounded by South Africa.

clue.text: Hearing again about shelter — time to turn over

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: to turn over says these combined letters are flipped end to end

parts.note: a lair is an animal's den or shelter

explanation.surface: A tenant, it seems, is told about their home and given time to hand it back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn over' joins with LAIR + T to give TRIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A retrial is a second court hearing of a case, the case heard afresh.
